items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s where I first heard or knew about King Oliver. ... I remember hearing him. I didn’t go in. I was just a child. I wasn’t allowed to go into the nightclub or see him at that stage in my life, but I could hear him.

ctx.x: Oh yes. I recall the first place we moved in was an apartment on 31st Street. It was in a building. In this building on the main floor was a nightclub, which they called a cabaret. In this cabaret King Oliver’s band played, and it had the signs in the lobby of this building that we lived in. That’s where I first heard or knew about King Oliver. We could hear the music when you came in. Like when the thing was going on, we could hear the music, go to rehearsals and that stuff, because it was right on the main…
This is where the cabaret was?
